text:
janet: Quick sync — need a final decision on the safety buffers and SLA wording for Dedicated GA. Can we lock numbers and the credit calc by EOD Friday? Open items below.

janet: Open items: 1) p99 latency SLO and acceptable tail buffer, 2) hard vs soft downtime (credit triggers), 3) canary/rollback behaviour & automated fallback, 4) pricing credits for incidents vs maintenance, 5) docs + runbooks + oncall playbook readiness.

miguel: From infra side — p95 200ms / p99 450ms looks achievable on current pools with batching tuned. Tail buffer +15% headroom seems reasonable during bursts.

miguel: If we pick tighter numbers we need to reserve extra capacity or limit burst autoscale. Not a showstopper but needs FinOps signoff.

aisha: Monitoring and alerting items: need separate alerts for "slo-deviation" vs "capacity-starved". Canary thresholds should be: error-rate > 0.5% OR p99 > threshold for 5m -> pause rollout.

aisha: Also require automated fallback policy: if canary fails, route to a compatible lower-cost variant automatically and notify ops.

tom: On credits — propose tiered credit calc: 

```
incident_duration_in_minutes = outage_end - outage_start
credit_pct = min(50, floor(incident_duration_in_minutes / 60) * 10)
```

tom: So 1 hour = 10% credit, 5+ hours = 50% cap. Differentiated for maintenance (no credits if pre-announced with 72h notice). Thoughts?

priya: Docs checklist: SLA.md draft, QuickStart-guide update with failover examples, Runbook: steps to toggle fallback + postmortem template. I can draft SLA wording once numbers are final.

janet: @miguel can you confirm whether the automatic fallback to quantized/cheaper model preserves request semantics (function calling, tooling)? If not, we need explicit dev warnings in the API and per-route opt-in.

miguel: Fallback preserves basic generation + streaming but may not support some heavy kernels (long-context keycache). We can make fallback compatible for common routes, but need to mark unsupported flags in telemetry and API returns.

priya: Will add an API-level warning snippet example and a short note in SDKs.

aisha: Oncall playbook: add a pre-flight checklist for rollouts (smoke queries, load ramp, canary observe window). Also require an immediate rollback playbook with exact commands.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started by miguel at 1758888900 — 12/24 nodes — monitoring p95/p99 per shard.

miguel: Canary: started, small noise at minute 8 — p99 spiked to 520ms for one shard, auto-fallback triggered for that shard and we rolled it back. No customer impact.

janet: Thanks — that confirms the fallback flow. This helps define the "automated fallback" clause.

tom: Pricing note: we should add a clause that credits do not apply to usage above committed capacity in Dedicated contracts (still chargeable), credits only reduce overage fees. That reduces financial exposure.

janet: Action items: 
- miguel: confirm final p95/p99 numbers + headroom plan by Thu EOD (1758975288).
- aisha: draft canary and oncall playbook snippets by Thu EOD.
- tom: finalize credit formula and contract language with legal by Fri midday.
- priya: draft SLA.md with placeholders for numbers and fallback text once numbers confirmed.

janet: If we align on these by Friday we can ship SLA language into the Dedicated contract and publish runbooks with the GA docs. :thumbsup:

miguel: Ack. I'll also add a telemetry flag so we can track when fallback occurs per-route.

aisha: I'll add alert runbooks to PagerDuty and a quick run-through with oncall tomorrow.

janet: Great. Re-open if anything slips. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
